definition: Prehension is the act or function of grasping or taking hold of something. In this historical usage, it refers especially to the hand’s capacity to serve as a refined organ for grasping as well as touch.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Anthropoid; pinned source text

reasons: The packet supports a historical anatomical sense in which the hand is an organ of prehension and touch, but it does not support the broader claim that prehension means the act or function of grasping or taking hold.

The wording “especially the hand’s capacity to serve as a refined organ for grasping as well as touch” goes beyond the source, which only describes the hand as a delicate organ of prehension and touch, not as an abstract functional definition.

The definition’s first sentence (“the act or function of grasping or taking hold of something”) is not explicitly supported by the packet; the packet only describes the hand as “a delicate organ of prehension and touch.”

The packet supports the historical sense component about the hand serving as an organ for “prehension and touch,” but it does not support the broader, non-anchored phrasing about “act or function of grasping or taking hold.”
Because one substantive claim is unsupported by the packet, the definition cannot be passed under the stated criteria.
